01 / Overview

Project memory for coding agents

A tool for recovering the reasons behind previous work in a new session. Session-end and pre-compaction hooks queue conversations; the selected recording model updates topic-based notes. Its instructions distinguish user decisions from agent proposals and retain scope and reasons for changes. Saved conversations let you check the result.

02 / FEATURES

Features

01

Conversation to memory

Claude Code and Codex hooks add sessions to a processing queue. Recording resumes from the last saved position.

02

Memory across tools

Store Markdown in a folder you choose and index it with qmd. Claude Code and Codex search the same memory through qmd MCP.

03

Traceable sources

Follow links from memory documents to saved conversation copies and individual statements.

04

Review and sync

Compare automatically recorded changes and select notes to commit. Review evidence, choices, and the final diff when histories diverge between PCs.

03 / INTERFACE

Inside the app

Select an image to view it at a larger size.

01 / 07

Current work and what needs attention

See active recording, waiting sessions, and recent activity from the tray. Connection problems and notes to review appear under Needs attention. The footer shows the last sync and lets you sync now.

02 / 07

Choose how notes are recorded

Select a model and its supported effort from the CLI’s list, or enter a model name when the list is unavailable. Settings apply as you change them. Choose a system, light, or dark appearance.

03 / 07

Inspect the files behind each connection

Manage Lore lists each tool’s MCP connection, memory guidance, search skill, and session hooks. Repair or disconnect clients and manage the memory folder, search index, and required tools in the same window.

04 / 07

Manage search on this PC

The recording model and the search embedding model have separate roles. Check collections and index paths, then confirm an embedding-model change before rebuilding this PC’s index.

05 / 07

Review conflicting decisions with their evidence

When histories diverge between PCs, inspect the changed notes and start a model comparison. Work through decisions in the sidebar with source quotations and available choices. Related changes are compared even without a Git line conflict.

06 / 07

Compare the result before applying it

After making your choices, compare the current note and the proposed result side by side. Apply & share confirms the merge, indexing, and push. Model comparisons can miss contradictions, so inspect the evidence and final wording.

07 / 07

Start with a guided connection

Explore a short memory example, choose your AI tools and memory folder, and prepare what this PC needs. Setup readiness is separate from successful recording and recall in an actual session.

05 / FAQ

Questions

Built with
Tauri 2RustReactTypeScriptqmdGit
Can I install it now?＋

Lore is in development. Public installers and source code are not available yet.

Will every agent automatically use the memory?＋

Later agents also need qmd MCP and instructions to search for memory. Recording and retrieval are separate steps.

Where are conversations and memory stored?＋

Documents and source conversation copies are kept in your selected memory folder. Queues, settings, and search indexes are stored separately in each computer’s app data.

Is all processing local?＋

Files and indexes are stored locally, but conversations and memory needed for recording are sent to the model provider used by your selected CLI.
